(`DashboardScreen.kt`, 9 `strings.xml`; RemEx-yrua.)
- **A file’s `using` block now lists only what that file actually reaches for.** All eight projects enable `ImplicitUsings`, so `System`, `System.Collections.Generic`, `System.IO`, `System.Linq`, `System.Net.Http`, `System.Threading` and `System.Threading.Tasks` were already in scope everywhere and 558 explicit imports across 234 files were restating them. **The bead’s premise needed correcting first, and getting it wrong would have broken the build**: it described `remex.agent` as ASP.NET-hosted and its web implicit set as redundant, but every project declares `Microsoft.NET.Sdk`, not `Microsoft.NET.Sdk.Web` — so `Microsoft.AspNetCore.*`, `Microsoft.Extensions.*` and `System.Net.Http.Json` are **not** implied here and had to stay. Only the base seven are. **The simpler of the two routes was taken deliberately.** The bead offered `dotnet format` with IDE0005 promoted, and warned it silently does nothing without `GenerateDocumentationFile` — meaning a clean run would have proved nothing at all. Removing the known set by name and letting the compiler adjudicate has no such failure mode. **Reviewability was this bead’s real concern, and the diff answers it without splitting into seven commits**: 585 deletions, **zero insertions**, and every deleted line is one of those seven strings or a blank left behind where a using block started with one. That is verifiable by script rather than by reading 234 files. Verified on both toolchains, since `Remex.Core` lost 103 lines and is also NativeAOT-linked for Android: `dotnet build -t:Rebuild` clean, 881 tests green, and `assembleRelease` relinked and synced a fresh `libRemexCore.so`. (234 `.cs` files across 7 projects; RemEx-4hpf.)
- **Two `ConnectionViewModel` properties that looked like dead code are documented as deliberately unbound, and checking why uncovered a defect class the new guard cannot see.** `HostRuntimeLabel` and `RemoteDesktopAvailabilitySummary` resolve localized text and appear in no view, which reads as dead twice over. **They are not**: the first is consumed by `AboutViewModel.UpdateHostVersion` and by `HostRuntimeSummary`, the second by `SettingsViewModel.UpdateHostCapabilitySummary` and `RemoteDesktopViewModel` — each surfacing it through their own bound property. The answer is now written at both declarations so the next scan that flags them costs a comment to dismiss rather than an investigation to repeat. **The investigation was worth more than its verdict.** These properties are read as *snapshots* into plain observable properties, and that is a second shape of the stale-label bug which `LocalizedPropertyRefreshTests` is blind to by construction: the bound property’s getter is a plain field read with no localizer call anywhere near it, so no getter-based scan can find it, while the user sees exactly the same staleness. `SettingsViewModel` has it for real and in the normal case — its locale handler refreshes `HostRuntimeText`/`HostCapabilityText` **only while disconnected**, so a connected user switching language keeps the old wording until host capabilities next change. `RemoteDesktopViewModel` has a milder instance in a transient status line. `AboutViewModel` gets it right and is recorded as the reference. All of it, plus the observation that its handler is the only one guarding against `SetCulture` raising three notifications per switch, is filed as RemEx-q3h0 with the fix for each site — kept out of this change because it is a different defect in different files, and folding it in would have hidden a real bug inside a documentation commit. 879 tests green, 0 warnings. (`ConnectionViewModel.cs`; RemEx-r5pm.)
- **The five non-home screens now inherit their card shape instead of being pinned to the universal clover.** App Launcher, Task Manager, Remote Desktop, Remote Control and Remote Mouse all defaulted to `18.0f` — the legacy clover — while the Home and telemetry buckets moved to `SHAPE_PRESET_INHERIT` in RemEx-km0i.7. The design spec deliberately scoped that migration to two buckets and asked for a follow-up; this is it. Thirteen fallbacks in `SettingsManager` changed: the data-class defaults, the individual preference flows and the combined-flow reads, all three of which had to move together or a screen would report one default on first read and another after a settings change. **The migration needed its own key, and that is the part worth recording.** `migrateShapeDefaultsV2` guards on `shape_defaults_migrated_v2`, which has already fired on every existing install — so adding the five new keys to its list would have migrated **new installs only**, leaving everyone else on the clover and the two populations silently disagreeing about what the default is. `migrateShapeDefaultsV3` has a separate key and runs alongside it. It is non-destructive in the same way V2 is: it rewrites only a value that is absent or still the legacy clover, so a user who deliberately chose `18.0f` for one of these screens keeps it. The two cases are indistinguishable in storage, and preserving a real choice matters more than migrating every last default. `assembleRelease` succeeds, unit tests pass. (`SettingsManager.kt`, `DashboardViewModel.kt`; RemEx-nkdv.)
- **The delay parser that decides how long before the PC shuts down existed twice, byte for byte, and is now one function.** `ParseDelaySeconds` was duplicated between `PingPongHandler` (the WebSocket ingress) and `RemexNetworkListener` (the TCP script ingress) — two copies of the code that reads how many seconds to wait before powering a machine down. That stays in sync right up until it does not: adding a fourth accepted key spelling, or changing the clamp, in one path would silently give the two transports different behaviour for the same command. **The two bodies were confirmed byte-identical before anything moved** — a whitespace-normalised comparison of the extracted method bodies, 270 characters each — so the hoist is provably behaviour-preserving rather than assumed to be. Both local copies are gone, ten call sites now resolve to `Remex.Core.Services.Command.CommandDelayParameter`, and the bare `315360000` became a named `MaxDelaySeconds` with the reason it exists written down: it is not a scheduling horizon but a bound that keeps a garbled value out of the platform's shutdown scheduler. Kept free of reflection and non-source-generated serialization, since `Remex.Core` is also compiled into `libRemexCore.so`. RemEx-xmgw stays open for its other two items, and its notes now flag that the second — deduping `AcceptSelfSignedCertificate` — is **certificate validation**, on CLAUDE.md's high-risk list, where the two copies must be diffed for real differences first: if they differ, the difference may be deliberate, and merging them would be a security change wearing a cleanup's clothes. 873 tests green, 0 warnings. (`CommandDelayParameter.cs`, `PingPongHandler.cs`, `RemexNetworkListener.cs`; RemEx-xmgw, partial.)
- **The PC drag-and-drop handlers moved off Avalonia's deprecated `IDataObject` API, and the search box no longer clears itself by writing a private field.** The solution built with nine warnings, in two unrelated families. Eight were `CS0618`: Avalonia 11.3 deprecated `DragEventArgs.Data`/`DataFormats.Files` in favour of `DragEventArgs.DataTransfer` and the generic `DataFormat.File` token, so the five drop sites in the launcher and file-transfer views now read files through `TryGetFiles()` — a typed accessor rather than the old cast-in-disguise — with identical accept/reject behaviour. The ninth, `MVVMTK0034`, was not cosmetic: `FileTransferViewModel.ClearSearch()` assigned the `[ObservableProperty]` backing field `_searchQuery` directly and then hand-raised the change notification, because `ClearSearch()` is itself called *from* `OnSearchQueryChanged` and going through the property would have re-entered it and run the search teardown twice. That workaround also skipped `PropertyChanging` entirely. It is now an explicit `_isClearingSearch` re-entrancy guard: the property setter is used normally, the callback short-circuits while the clear is in flight, and the intent is documented where the next reader will look for it instead of being implied by a field write. No user-visible behaviour change on any path — the search TextBox still receives the cleared value, and whitespace-only or unsupported-root queries still reset to the folder view. Full rebuild is now warning-free in production code; the four remaining `xUnit1031` warnings are in a test file and are filed separately rather than folded into this diff. 811 tests green. (`AppLauncherView.axaml.cs`, `FileTransferView.axaml.cs`, `FileTransferViewModel.cs`; RemEx-5c37.)
- **The file-manager protocol parsing existed twice; now it exists once.** `ShareToPcViewModel` re-implemented `FileTransferViewModel`'s response parsing — two copies of the same field reads for shared roots and directory entries — now extracted into `FileManagerLogic.parseSharedRoots` / `parseFileEntries`, with each screen still mapping onto its own model. **The risk in a dedupe like this is the error handling, not the parsing:** the two callers were *not* symmetric (`FileTransferViewModel` checks `errorMessage` before parsing, `ShareToPcViewModel` never did), and that asymmetry is preserved deliberately rather than unified, because "make both do the stricter thing" is a behaviour change wearing a refactor's clothing. Whether the share screen *should* check `errorMessage` is a real question and a different bead. New tests pin the two cases most likely to drift later: a null JSON array yielding an empty list rather than throwing, and a missing boolean defaulting to false. (`ShareToPcViewModel.kt`, `FileTransferViewModel.kt`, `FileManagerLogic.kt`, `FileManagerLogicTest.kt`; RemEx-4xhj.)
- **The remote-desktop MJPEG fallback repaints frames in place instead of rebuilding the image node every frame.** The fallback path wrapped its `Image` in `key(currentFrameTimestamp)`, so every incoming frame tore down and rebuilt the entire node — layout, `graphicsLayer` transform and modifier chain — just to force a redraw. A `Canvas` at a stable call site is reused across frames and only the draw phase reads the new bitmap, using the screen's own `contentRect()` letterbox math (already documented as producing the same fitted rect `ContentScale.Fit` did) so input mapping and the cursor overlay stay pixel-aligned; the frame's content description is preserved via `semantics`. H.264 (the primary path) is untouched. (`RemoteDesktopScreen.kt`; RemEx-ki0t.)
- **Launcher app icons decode off the main thread, through one helper instead of two copies.** `AppGridItem` and `RecentAppCarousel` each carried a near-identical `remember { Base64.decode + BitmapFactory.decodeByteArray }` block that ran on the main thread during first composition of every grid item. Both now call a single `rememberAppIconBitmap(iconBase64)` that decodes via `produceState` on `Dispatchers.Default`, returning null (and thus the fallback launch icon) for missing or corrupt data instead of crashing or leaving a blank tile. (`AppLauncherScreen.kt`; RemEx-f076.)
- **Cancelling a file transfer no longer does ContentResolver I/O on the caller's thread.** `FileTransferEngine.cancel()` ran its empty-download-target cleanup (a `query` + `deleteDocument`) synchronously on whatever thread invoked it — often the main thread, from a UI cancel button. The cleanup now hops onto the engine's own long-lived scope, which also survives the caller's coroutine being mid-cancellation; a `withContext` there would have silently skipped the cleanup in exactly that case. (`FileTransferEngine.kt`; RemEx-cuiq.)
- **Twelve host constructors now fail fast with a named `ArgumentNullException` instead of storing a null dependency.** Required non-nullable dependencies were assigned bare (`_logger = logger;`), so a missing DI registration surfaced later as an opaque `NullReferenceException` from wherever the field was first dereferenced — often on a background thread far from the real cause. They now go through `Guard.NotNull` per the CLAUDE.md null-safety convention, which names the offending parameter via `[CallerArgumentExpression]`. Two constructors gain a real robustness win beyond the diagnostics: `RemoteDesktopHandler` and `WindowsDisplayPowerMonitor` now validate *before* starting their long-running input-queue and message-pump threads, so a bad dependency no longer leaks a live thread. Optional nullable parameters are deliberately left unguarded — guarding them would turn an optional dependency into a hard failure, and in one case would have been fatal: `WindowsScreenCaptureService`'s `IWgcCaptureSource? wgc` is passed as literal `null` by the delegating constructor and resolved with `GetService` (not `GetRequiredService`), so guarding it would have crashed host startup on every build without the WGC project. `RemexNetworkListener`'s `certificateService`/`authenticator` are likewise left bare. The two pairing-flow sites (`PairingService`, `PairingHandler`) were done under explicit operator sign-off and are strictly constructor-assignment edits — the handshake, PIN generation and verification, HMAC computation, session lifetime, and brute-force throttle are byte-identical, verified line-by-line against HEAD by an adversarial review specifically tasked with finding a way to brick pairing. No behavior change on any valid startup path; 790 tests green including 51 pairing tests. Reviewed by Opus (PASS, both rounds). (`RemexNetworkListener.cs`, `ExternalNetworkListenerService.cs`, `MdnsAdvertisingService.cs`, `LinuxCaptureSessionLifetime.cs`, `FFmpegH264Encoder.cs`, `WindowsDisplayPowerMonitor.cs`, `DxgiDesktopCapture.cs`, `HostCapabilitiesProvider.cs`, `RemoteDesktopHandler.cs`, `PairingService.cs`, `PairingHandler.cs`, `WindowsScreenCaptureService.cs`; RemEx-2gl8, RemEx-wpfo.)
- **Bold text is now driven by named emphasized typography roles instead of 60+ ad-hoc weight overrides.** The same visual rank used to get a different weight on different screens (`titleMedium` was SemiBold in 6 places, Bold in 3, Black in 1). `typographyForFontFamily` now builds all 15 M3 `*Emphasized` roles with the app's canonical emphasis weight per role (majority-wins from the pre-migration inventory, ties resolved to SemiBold) — built alongside the base roles so they carry the user's font family and in-app scale, which `Typography.copy()` would otherwise silently drop. 63 call sites migrated to the emphasized roles; base roles are untouched, so plain text renders identically. 18 minority-weight sites shift slightly to their role's canonical weight (e.g. the Personalization section headers Black→SemiBold, WAKE PC Bold→SemiBold). Four deliberate literals remain (AC budget ≤5): two telemetry hero values and the connection orb label at display-weight Black, and one link `SpanStyle` — plus three dynamic-weight conditionals (lock-state chip, directory-vs-file rows) that can't be a single static role. Reviewed by Opus (round-2 PASS; round 1 caught three deeply-line-wrapped sites the migration script missed). (`Type.kt` + 21 screen/component files; RemEx-0855.)

### Changed (docs/tooling)
- **Every silent exception swallow in the C# codebase now says why it is silent — all 43 of them, verified to zero.** A bare `catch { }` is indistinguishable from an oversight, so the question a reader has ("is this deliberate, or did someone give up?") had no answer anywhere in the source. Each site now records what actually throws and why swallowing is the right response. **They are site-specific by necessity, not by preference:** a generic "silent fail" comment repeated 43 times would look like the work was done while telling the next reader nothing, and would actively discourage them from investigating. So the process monitors explain that `WorkingSet64`, `TotalProcessorTime` and `MainModule` are refused for processes at a higher integrity level and that the row is still worth listing with one field absent; the streaming teardowns explain that they just cancelled the task and the exception is its acknowledgement; the JNI cleanups explain that a socket which fails to dispose is already unusable and throwing would replace the real pairing outcome with a teardown error; and the input router explains that a backend failing to probe is the normal case on a system that does not have it. **The bead's count was low — 35 claimed, 43 real** — and the gap is the useful part: the obvious grep for `catch { }` misses every typed form and anything the formatter has wrapped. A detector matching a catch whose body contains neither a statement nor a comment found them all, and is recorded on the bead so the count can be re-derived rather than trusted. It also caught a mistake mid-way: the first batch of comments went *above* the catch, which builds fine, reads fine in a diff, and leaves `catch (X) { }` still looking unexplained — the detector kept counting them, which is how the placement got corrected to inside the braces. 873 tests green, 0 warnings. (14 files across `remex.agent`, `remex.core`, `remex.desktop` and both test projects; RemEx-t4tc.)
- **The two process monitors' twelve silent exception swallows now say why they are silent.** A bare `catch { }` is indistinguishable from an oversight, and these sit in the code that builds the Task Manager listing — so the question "is this deliberate?" had no answer in the file. Each now records what actually throws and why swallowing is correct: `WorkingSet64`, `TotalProcessorTime` and `MainModule` are all refused for processes at a higher integrity level (which is most of the ones worth protecting), `/proc` entries vanish mid-enumeration as a matter of routine on a busy machine, and in every case the **row** is still worth listing with one field absent — dropping it would hide a running process from the user entirely. **Placement turned out to matter, and the first attempt got it wrong.** The comments initially went *above* each catch, which builds fine and reads fine in a diff but leaves `catch (X) { }` still looking unexplained to anyone scanning the file. They are now inside the braces, where the reader's eye actually lands. **The bead's count was low — 35 claimed, 43 real** — and the gap is instructive: the obvious grep for `catch { }` misses the typed forms and anything the formatter has wrapped. A detector that matches a catch whose body contains neither a statement nor a comment found the rest, and is recorded on the bead as the way to measure the remaining 31 rather than trusting a number. Also recorded: the annotations have to be site-specific or they are worse than nothing — a generic "silent fail" on 43 sites would look like the work was done while telling the next reader nothing, and would discourage them from looking. 873 tests green, 0 warnings. (`WindowsProcessMonitorService.cs`, `LinuxProcessMonitorService.cs`; RemEx-t4tc, partial.)
- **The JNI boundary now documents its contract, not its method names.** `JniHelper` is the hand-rolled bridge the Android app loads as `libRemexCore.so`, and every call in it reaches Java through the JNI function table **by ordinal** — the magic numbers in each body are spec-fixed indices. That is the load-bearing fact and it was written nowhere: a wrong index is not a compile error and not an exception, it is a call through a mistyped function pointer, which is undefined behaviour and usually a process abort with no managed stack. Two other rules govern everything in the file and are now stated once at the top rather than rediscovered per method: **no JNI call may run while a Java exception is pending** — the runtime aborts with SIGABRT rather than reporting an error, which is why the string helpers check and clear — and **every reference JNI hands back is local**, valid only until the native call returns, so anything kept beyond that needs promoting and releasing. The per-member docs say what a reader cannot infer: which functions return a reference the caller must release, that `GetMethodID` takes a JVM descriptor rather than a Java signature and fails by leaving a pending exception so the *next* call aborts, why the boolean overload of `CallVoidMethod` exists at all (JNI passes arguments by exact primitive width, so routing a bool through the object overload corrupts the call frame rather than failing to compile), and that `AndroidLogE` deliberately bypasses JNI because it is what still works when the JNI path itself is broken. **The bead's inventory was wrong in both directions and is corrected in its notes.** It claims 485 undocumented members; measured against the tree it is 319 of 556, now 301. And its first-priority item — the interfaces — is already done: `IFileTrustService` has docs on all seven members. The measured hotspot list, and a reusable way to produce it, are recorded so the next pass starts from the real numbers. 873 tests green, 0 warnings. (`JniHelper.cs`; RemEx-cnwu, partial.)
- **Build hygiene: an orphaned package pin removed and `ImplicitUsings` aligned.** `Directory.Packages.props` still pinned `Microsoft.Extensions.Hosting.WindowsServices`, a leftover of the removed Windows Service architecture, referenced by zero projects. And `remex.desktop` was the only one of nine projects without `ImplicitUsings` — an odd split given it compiles into `remex.agent`, so the two halves of one process disagreed. Enabling it was the item with actual risk, since implicit usings can surface `CS0104` ambiguities in an Avalonia project; none materialised. Existing explicit usings in that project are now redundant rather than wrong, which is the orphaned-using sweep's job. The `xunit.runner.visualstudio` bump the same bead asked for is split out: only the current version is in the local NuGet cache, so choosing a target needs a restore this machine cannot confirm. (`Directory.Packages.props`, `remex.desktop.csproj`; RemEx-woc0.)

- **Code comments no longer describe a Windows service, a Session-0 host, or a separate desktop client as the current design.** Seventeen sites across `remex.agent`, `remex.core` and `remex.desktop` still presented the pre-2.0 process model as live — a Session-0 command agent paired with a separate GUI host, a LocalSystem service, "the desktop client". That model has been gone since RemEx-aep; there is one elevated process in the signed-in user's session that is both host and UI, and Android is the only client. This matters beyond tidiness: CLAUDE.md exists partly because these comments have repeatedly misled contributors into designing around components that do not exist. Rationale comments kept their history rather than losing it — the reason `cert.pfx` and pairing state live in machine-wide `ProgramData` really *was* the LocalSystem service, and machine-wide storage is still deliberate, so those now read as "originally X, still correct because Y". Three of the seventeen were not comments at all but text shown to the operator, including one that told a non-technical user to *"configure the Windows service to log on as that user"*; those now say plainly that RemEx must be running in a signed-in session and normally starts on its own. The two independent copies of that message — the primary diagnostic and its fallback — were made identical so they can no longer contradict each other. Comments-only otherwise: no code, signatures or behaviour changed. Reviewed by Opus (round-2 PASS; round 1 correctly failed an incomplete sweep, catching a fixed comment whose verbatim twin was left stale and an edit that contradicted a line eight rows above it). (16 files; RemEx-k521.)

- **`AGENTS.md` rewritten lean (647 → 357 lines) with all 2.0-era history archived to `docs/OLD DOCS/AGENTS-2.0-archive.md`.** The frozen 2.0 Release Gate tables, closed-work narratives, and a duplicate machine-managed Beads block are gone from the live file; the durable do-not-regress rules embedded in those narratives (WinRT `FromAbi`/IID marshaling, `PrecisionPacer`/`DuplicationReinitThrottle` routing, `h264_nvenc_bgra`-only GPU encode, sender-scoped `OpenPipeWireRemote`, warm portal session, SurfaceView `Modifier.layout` invariant, and more) are distilled into a new "Carry-Forward Rules" section. (RemEx-79j3.)
- **`CLAUDE.md` no longer instructs agents to read per-project `AGENTS.md` files that don't exist**, points global instructions at the real `~/.claude/AGENTS.md` (there is no global `CLAUDE.md`), and marks `agy`/`agy-splitter` as external tools to verify before use. (RemEx-79j3.)

### Removed
- **`scripts/fix-host-install.ps1`, which could not have worked.** It existed to repair a "split-brain" install — a LocalSystem `RemexHost` service pointing at the repo's publish folder while an HKCU Run key launched a *second*, different build from Program Files, the two colliding on the shared port and IPC pipes. **Neither half of that situation can occur now**: RemEx-aep deleted the Windows Service, and `remex.agent` is a single elevated process in the signed-in session started by a logon task. **It was also broken, not merely obsolete.** Its `-StageDir` defaulted to `artifacts\stage_8bn`, a one-off staging directory from the session that wrote it, which does not exist — so the invocation printed in the script's own `.EXAMPLE` fails immediately at the "Staged build not found" check. Every remaining useful step is already done better elsewhere and was verified rather than assumed: `autostart-remex.ps1` removes the legacy `RemexHost` service on **both** Install and Uninstall (not just one), and deploy-plus-restart is `update-local-install.ps1`. Nothing referenced it — `remex.agent.csproj` globs `..\scripts\**` so it was copied to build output incidentally, and `installer/RemEx.iss` names only `autostart-remex.ps1`, meaning **it never reached an end user at all**. Deleting rather than keeping it behind a "legacy only" header was the call because a header on a script whose documented invocation fails is an invitation to a confusing five minutes; git history keeps it recoverable. The two 2026-06-18 `session-keep-unlocked` design documents were annotated as superseded in the same pass, but `docs/superpowers/` is gitignored, so that annotation is local to a working copy and is deliberately not force-added — a fresh clone has no such files and therefore no stale-architecture hazard to fix. (RemEx-6cdy.)

- **Two localized strings that no user could ever see, in all nine languages.** `screen_splash_title` and `screen_tutorial_title` existed solely to satisfy the mandatory-`titleRes` constructor described above — the splash and tutorial screens appear in no navigation surface, so nothing read either value. Each key was verified to have exactly one reference in the tree, the `NavRoutes.kt` argument itself, before deletion; 18 values in total. `qr_scanner_title`, `screen_connection_title` and `pairing_title` were deliberately **kept**, because each has a second consumer that renders it as that screen's own heading — being absent from the nav bar is not the same as being untitled, and the KDoc now says so to stop the accessibility bug being re-filed. (9 `strings.xml`; RemEx-5reo.)

- **53 genuinely unused imports removed across both platforms — and getting the count right took two corrections that are worth more than the removals.** 47 Kotlin imports and 6 C# usings. **The first detector reported 602 Kotlin imports as unused, which was the tell.** It excluded any name appearing after a dot, and Compose imports are overwhelmingly *extension functions* used exactly there — `Modifier.padding(...)`. Every one of them looked dead. A 14× discrepancy against a hand-audited number is a reason to distrust the tool, not the bead. **The second correction came from the compiler.** With the lookbehind fixed the count fell to 91, still too high, and applying it broke the build on `import androidx.compose.runtime.getValue` — because `val x by state` invokes `getValue` as an *operator convention*, by syntax rather than by name, so no name-based check can ever see it. Excluding the operator family (`getValue`, `setValue`, `invoke`, `plus`, `get`, `compareTo` and the rest) brought it to 47, essentially matching the bead's hand-audited ~44. **The bead was also wrong in the opposite direction on one C# entry**, despite claiming token-level verification: it lists `X509Certificates` in `RemexDesktopClient.cs` as unused, but `X509Certificate2` is used at line 99 — the build caught it and the using was restored. The remaining half of the bead, usings made redundant by `ImplicitUsings`, is split out: those are harmless rather than wrong, and folding dozens of files of no-op churn into this diff would have buried 53 real removals. `assembleRelease` succeeds, 873 tests green, 0 warnings. (20 Kotlin files, 5 C# files; RemEx-cm7b.)
- **All 233 orphaned PC localization keys are gone — 1108 base keys down to 875, and the localization baseline shrank with them.** These were the residue of features that no longer exist: the removed Windows Service, pre-rename `Shell_*` and `Home_*` leftovers, retired tooltips, an old boot sequence, superseded file-transfer and navigation sets. 2097 values across nine locale files, plus 133 accessors in the checked-in `Strings.Designer.cs`. **The deletions were the easy part; the audit that made them safe is the substance.** The bead named three key families that are assembled at runtime and are therefore invisible to a reference scan. There are six. Grepping for every *non-literal* `LocalizationService.Instance[...]` lookup — instead of trusting the list — found `EnumLocalizerConverter` composing `$"{TypeName}_{Value}"`, which hides every member of every localized enum, and `PrefixedLabelConverter` composing `prefix + id` with `Custom_BgType_` and `Custom_Scheme_`. Those 17 keys survive; deleting them would have made the personalization panel and the alert UI render **raw key names in every language**, with no build error, because `LocalizationService`'s indexer ends in `?? key`. **Prefix is a hint, not a verdict.** `Service_*` is the removed Windows Service and looked entirely dead — two of its 38 keys are still live, repurposed for a host-unavailable message. The purge asserted on referenced keys rather than proceeding, which is why that was caught rather than shipped. **And the Designer file is checked in, not generated**, so a deleted key whose accessor survives compiles cleanly and returns null at runtime; the accessors went in the same pass. Every deleted value is recorded verbatim first, all 2097 of them. Verified from both ends: the orphan detector now reports zero, the localization check reports no new problems, and its baseline dropped 361 → 270 because 91 of those suppressed findings were staleness warnings about keys that no longer exist. 873 tests green, 0 warnings. (9 resx + `Strings.Designer.cs`; RemEx-b5kx.)
- **The removed Windows Service's 36 leftover localization keys are gone — and finding them safely exposed three gaps in the audit that produced this task.** The bead lists three families that are built at runtime and must never be purged by a literal search. There are at least six. Grepping for every non-literal `LocalizationService.Instance[...]` lookup, rather than trusting the list, turned up `EnumLocalizerConverter` composing `$"{TypeName}_{Value}"` — which makes **every member of every localized enum** invisible to a reference scan — and `PrefixedLabelConverter` composing `prefix + id`, used from the personalization panel with `Custom_BgType_` and `Custom_Scheme_`. That is 17 keys which a prefix-and-grep purge would have deleted, after which the personalization panel and the alert UI would have rendered **raw key names in every language**, because `LocalizationService`'s indexer ends in `?? key`. **A second lesson came from the family that looked safest.** `Service_*` is the removed Windows Service, which CLAUDE.md confirms is gone — and two of its 38 keys are still live, repurposed for a host-unavailable message. The script asserted on referenced keys rather than proceeding, which is the only reason that was caught; it now filters rather than assumes. **A third: the Designer file is checked in, not generated.** `Strings.Designer.cs` holds 305 hand-maintained accessors, so a deleted key whose accessor survives compiles cleanly and returns null at runtime — 34 accessors were removed alongside. The corrected orphan count is **233**, not the ~243 the bead states nor the 249 a naive scan reports, and the method to re-derive it is recorded rather than the number. 873 tests green, 0 warnings, localization check clean. (9 resx + `Strings.Designer.cs`; RemEx-b5kx, partial.)
- **Eight dead `OperatingSystem.IsAndroid()` branches removed from the PC app — and one of them was hiding a silent data-loss bug.** `remex.desktop` targets `net10.0`, not `net10.0-android`, so those calls can never return true; RemEx-f167 established that and left the reasoning in the source. **The interesting one was the catch block.** `DashboardLayoutService.SaveInternalAsync` ended in `catch (Exception ex) { if (OperatingSystem.IsAndroid()) { Debug.WriteLine(...); } }` — so a failed dashboard-layout save has been reporting *nothing at all*, because its only diagnostic sat behind an unreachable guard. Deleting the dead branch mechanically, which is what "remove dead code" invites, would have left a bare `catch (Exception ex) { }`: a genuine silent swallow where the user loses their customised layout with no indication, and a clean build either way. The guard is gone and **the diagnostic kept**, so it now actually runs. It remains a stopgap — `Debug.WriteLine` compiles out of Release — and the real fix is recorded on RemEx-t4tc with the constraint that matters: the service is constructed directly in tests, so an `ILogger` has to be optional with a `NullLogger` fallback rather than required. The other seven were straightforward once each shape was handled on its own terms: two ternaries collapsed to their reachable branch, an Android-only immediate-save path and a widget-update subscription deleted outright, a success-path trace deleted rather than un-gated (un-gating would log on every save), and two `!IsAndroid() && X` Settings conditions collapsed to `X` — those two gate whole Settings sections, so getting them wrong would have silently hidden or shown a settings area. The only mentions left in the assembly are the two comments explaining why the calls are gone. 873 tests green, 0 warnings. (`DashboardLayoutService.cs`, `App.axaml.cs`, `SettingsViewModel.cs`; RemEx-eca6.)
- **Seven verified-dead symbols removed from both platforms, each re-proved dead against the current tree first.** `DetermineCategory` (26 lines), `FrameSendTimeout`, `SM_CXSCREEN`, `SM_CYSCREEN`, `GetImmediateContextFn`, `PinLength` and the Kotlin `RepeatingIconButton` composable (24 lines) are gone. The bead said to confirm each with a fresh reference search before removal, and that mattered: a whitespace-tolerant word-boundary search across **517 files** — every `.cs`, `.kt` and `.axaml` in agent, core, desktop, android and all three test projects — found exactly one occurrence of each, the declaration itself, and zero uses; the same search returns zero for all seven afterwards. Word-boundary rather than plain substring matters here for the reason this repo has been bitten by twice: ktfmt wraps long references across lines, so a naive qualified-form search can report a live symbol as dead. **One thing the search could not have caught, and the build did:** removing the Kotlin composable left an **orphaned `@Composable` annotation** behind, which then sat stacked on the next function's own — `assembleRelease` failed with "This annotation is not repeatable". A reference search proves a symbol is unused; it says nothing about the decorations attached to it. Deleting a declaration means taking its annotations with it, and the release build is the check that notices. The bead's `PairingService` caveat ("file has uncommitted security work — coordinate") was stale; the tree was clean. Its notes' addendum — dead `OperatingSystem.IsAndroid()` branches — said six; there are **eight**, including two in `SettingsViewModel` the note missed, and they are split into RemEx-eca6 with the per-shape transformations spelled out, since two of them gate visible Settings sections. 873 tests green, 0 warnings, `assembleRelease` successful. (`WindowsTelemetryService.cs`, `RemoteDesktopHandler.cs`, `WindowsInputSimulationService.cs`, `DxgiDesktopCapture.cs`, `PairingService.cs`, `RemoteDesktopScreen.kt`; RemEx-xkmn.)
- **Eighteen more dead Android strings deleted, two kept as evidence of missing features, and three handed to the bead that already owned them.** This was the half of the unreferenced-key audit that a sweep explicitly *cannot* resolve, because for these an unreferenced key can be evidence of an absent code path rather than of dead weight — so every one was adjudicated individually against the code that should have referenced it. **The first finding was that the bead's own list was wrong:** its title said nineteen keys and its description enumerated seventeen, while a fresh sweep found **twenty-three**. Six had never been listed at all. That is now recorded as method: derive the set from the base `strings.xml` minus a bare-token scan, rather than working from a list written earlier. Of the twenty-three, eighteen had a live replacement or no surviving control. The most interesting was `permission_local_network_rationale`, which the bead flagged as a likely real gap — a local-network prompt appearing with no rationale is exactly the kind users deny by default. It was not: `ACCESS_LOCAL_NETWORK` is declared, requested at `ConnectionScreen.kt:164`, and a denial *is* explained, through the live key `error_local_network_permission_denied`. The six mouse keycap labels were the other trap, since the bead warned they might be what RemEx-qykh needed rather than strings to delete — qykh has since closed and did not want them, having used the `cd_*` and `remote_mouse_*` families instead, and no middle mouse button exists in the UI at all, so that pair had nothing to label. The three task-manager column headers were superseded by the sort-chip row, and RemEx-k0vy — which the bead said to check — is about that *chip* row failing at 1.4× font scale and does not want them back. **Two keys were deliberately kept, because for them the bead's premise held exactly.** `file_transfer_rename_timeout` is the fingerprint of a missing branch: `runManage()` is shared by delete, rename, copy, move and mkdir, and its timeout branch returns the *delete-specific* message for every one of them — while `renameEntry` discards the returned string anyway, so a rename that timed out and a rename the host refused produce the identical sentence. That evidence went to RemEx-201d, along with something not previously recorded there: a *mkdir* timeout surfaces the literal words "New folder failed: Delete timed out.", because `createFolder` interpolates the returned string raw. Copy and move do not — `manageSelectedTo` discards it into an error counter and reports a generic tally, which is its own flattening but not a wrong-operation message. `file_transfer_read_only_root` is the second: `canWrite` is computed at `FileTransferScreen.kt:113` and gates controls at `:227` and `:267`, but labels nothing, so selecting a read-only folder disables upload, paste, rename and delete with no explanation — filed as RemEx-dc57. The three pairing and QR strings were already owned by RemEx-ra2m, so they were handed over with their evidence rather than deferred as a duplicate. Base `values/` goes 747 → 729 strings; all nine locales carried all eighteen, so 162 elements were removed with the base-vs-locale parity difference unchanged. Every deleted English value is recorded verbatim on the bead before deletion. `assembleRelease` succeeds and the localization check reports no new problems. (9 `strings.xml`; RemEx-hgdb.)
- **Twelve dead Android strings deleted — 108 values gone from the translation surface, with every one recorded first.** These were the "probably genuinely dead" group of an unreferenced-key audit, and the point of the work was the **spot check**, not the sweep: an unreferenced key can be evidence of a *missing feature* rather than dead weight, which is how RemEx-x5dx got filed as an accessibility bug when it was really a cleanup. Each of these turned out to be a supersession. `splash_app_name` duplicates the live `app_name`; `snackbar_setup_connection` duplicates the live `button_setup_connection`; `settings_tab_about` is a leftover from when About was a Settings tab, and its five siblings are all still live while About is now its own screen; and `about_version_android` / `about_version_pc` are older combined formats replaced by the live `about_android_client_label` / `about_pc_host_label`. Verification used the method this repo has now proved twice — a whitespace-normalised **bare-token** sweep, never the qualified `R.string.KEY` form that ktfmt line-wrapping defeats (that false positive already caused one wrong deletion), plus a check that `getIdentifier` is absent so nothing can be reached by runtime name concatenation, which is what makes a static sweep exhaustive rather than merely indicative. `assembleRelease` passes including `lintVitalRelease`, which would flag a referenced-but-missing resource. All 108 values are recorded verbatim on the bead before deletion, because RemEx-paa7's first recovery note named the wrong English string and had to be corrected against git. Android is now 747 base strings and 745 per locale. The remaining nineteen unreferenced keys are deliberately untouched and split out as RemEx-hgdb: three are pairing-adjacent, where a missing reference plausibly means that failure reaches the user with no explanation at all, and sixteen look like genuine gaps — including six keycap labels that may be exactly what RemEx-qykh needs rather than strings to delete. (9 `strings.xml`; RemEx-a7n4.)
- **Two Android strings that cannot be translated no longer pretend to be translatable — and four that look identical are deliberately left alone.** A mechanical filter over all 759 base strings — strip the printf specifiers, keep whatever has no letter left in any script — yields six candidates, and all six are byte-identical across all nine locales today. **That second fact is a trap, not a confirmation:** identical-today can equally mean nobody has translated it yet, and `translatable="false"` is a one-way door that stops lint flagging the key and stops a translator overriding it. Only two are genuinely safe. `file_manager_transfer_active` is `"%1$s"` — a pure passthrough with no punctuation, spacing or unit, so there is nothing any language could want to change. `file_transfer_service_progress` already carried the attribute but was still copied into all eight locale files, so it was being ignored in practice; the copies are gone and the attribute now means something. The four left translatable are the interesting half: `cd_percent_value` is `"%1$d%%"`, and **French typography puts a narrow no-break space before the percent sign**, so freezing it would permanently lock in an error that simply has not been fixed yet; `cd_degree_value` is the same family; `file_transfer_progress_status` uses ASCII `...` where several locale files in this repo already prefer a real ellipsis elsewhere; and `dashboard_no_value` is listed as probably-dead by RemEx-a7n4, so marking a key about to be deleted would be churn. The rule this establishes is recorded on the bead: the mechanical filter finds *candidates*, it does not decide — a string qualifies only when there is nothing a translator could legitimately want to change, which for anything carrying a percent sign, an ellipsis, a unit or spacing around punctuation is almost never true. Six candidates, two safe. The eight "translated an invariant" warnings the localization check had been reporting are now gone, and parity reports clean with `-NoBaseline`. `assembleRelease` passes including `lintVitalRelease`. (8 `strings.xml`; RemEx-0uuq.)
- **The command palette's "Wake on LAN" entry is gone, because it had never once worked.** It bound a command that sent `WakeOnLan` with **no parameters**, on a code comment guessing the host "might use defaults". It does not: both dispatchers — `PingPongHandler`'s `/ws` branch and `RemexNetworkListener`'s 8338 TCP script channel — return `"Missing MacAddress parameter."` when no MAC is supplied. And the caller discarded the result tuple, so it failed **silently on every invocation since it was written**. There is a second, independent reason it could never work: `SendCommandAsync` returns `"Not connected"` before sending anything, so in the one case anybody invokes Wake-on-LAN for — the PC is off — it never reached a dispatcher at all. **Wake-on-LAN itself is untouched and still works fully from the Remote screen**, which has what the palette entry lacked: the configured MAC address, validation, and a local-send fallback for when there is no connection to send *through*. Repairing the entry rather than removing it was considered and rejected as a design change beyond a bugfix — `ShellViewModel` builds `RemoteViewModel` lazily on first navigation while the palette captures its commands once at construction, so the palette cannot reach the working command without either eager startup construction or late command resolution, and even then it would report into a status line only the Remote screen renders. Making the entry merely *navigate* was also rejected, on review's argument that the palette already has a Remote Control entry doing exactly that, so a second entry labelled with an action it does not perform would be a worse defect than the silent one it replaced. The orphaned `Palette_WakeOnLan` key was removed from all 9 files (1101 → 1100) with all nine values recorded verbatim on RemEx-efse, which also carries the one regression this creates: typing "wake" in the palette now matches nothing, because the filter searches labels and categories only — the cheap fix being a search alias on the existing Remote Control entry rather than a new command. (`CommandPaletteViewModel.cs`, `ConnectionViewModel.cs`, 9 resx files; RemEx-paa7.)
- **A dead Android string that was filed as a translation bug turned out to need deleting, not translating.** `connection_required_context` ("Connection required to access this feature.") sat as raw English in `values-es`, `-fr`, `-hi`, `-in` and `-pt-rBR` while `pl`, `tr` and `uk` carried real translations — so the new English-similarity detector (RemEx-km0i.20) flagged it, correctly. The inference drawn from that flag was wrong: nobody has ever seen the string in any language, because it is referenced nowhere. It is the un-parameterised ancestor of `disconnected_requires_connection` ("%1$s requires a connected PC.", live in `CommonComponents.kt`), which is strictly better because it *names* the feature instead of saying "this feature" — a supersession, not a gap. Removed from all 9 files (753 → 752 strings per locale, parity exact), and the 5 similarity entries dropped out of `scripts/localization-baseline.json` (381 → 376). **This is the second time this repo has misread a dead key as an untranslated one** — RemEx-x5dx was filed as an accessibility bug for the same reason — and RemEx-a7n4 had already classified this exact key as "probably genuinely dead, safe to delete after a spot check"; this was that spot check. Two verification lessons were recorded on that bead for its remaining 31 keys: a bare-token sweep is only exhaustive if nothing resolves resources dynamically, so `getIdentifier` must be confirmed absent (it is) — `lintVitalRelease` cannot close that hole, since it proves only that nothing referenced the key *statically* — and the sweep must cover `.pro`, `.gradle`, `AndroidManifest.xml`, navigation and theme XML, not just Kotlin and layouts. The qualified `R.string.KEY` grep remains banned: ktfmt line-wrapping makes it report live keys as dead, which already caused one wrong deletion. `assembleRelease` passes including the fatal `lintVitalRelease` gate. Reviewed by Opus (PASS). (9 `strings.xml`, `scripts/localization-baseline.json`; RemEx-9lsr.)
- **Four `Strings.Designer.cs` accessors outlived their resource keys.** `Settings_AccessKey`, `Settings_AccessKeyTooltip`, `Settings_AccessKeyWatermark` and `Shell_AccessKeyWatermark` were deleted from the `.resx` files earlier but their generated C# properties remained. They compiled fine and returned `null` at runtime, which surfaces as an empty label rather than an error — a trap for the next reader, who would see what looks like live API. Verified by diffing the full accessor set against the resx keys: 309 → 305 properties, zero orphans remaining, and zero references to any of the four. Doing this *before* the large orphaned-key purges (RemEx-b5kx, ~284 keys) matters, since deleting keys without regenerating this file would multiply the same trap. (RemEx-t9u8.)
- **The Connection help sheet no longer gives macOS IP-lookup instructions.** `remex.agent` ships for Windows and Linux only, so the sheet's macOS row pointed users at a platform that cannot run the PC side. This finishes what RemEx-oq6l (FAQ) and RemEx-hqcl (tutorial) started, on the last surface that still had a macOS block. The now-orphaned `connection_platform_macos` / `connection_ip_macos` keys are deliberately left in all 9 locales for the RemEx-a7n4/RemEx-3jne orphan triage, so key-set parity is untouched here. (`ConnectionScreen.kt`; RemEx-j1sp.)
- **Eight dead localization keys deleted, and two beads closed as stale rather than "fixed".** A parallel sweep of ten low-risk beads, grouped so no two agents touched the same file. PC: `Tooltip_GlassOpacity` / `Tooltip_GlassOpacitySlider` (RemEx-yho8) and the four pre-2.0 Access Key strings `Settings_AccessKey` / `_AccessKeyTooltip` / `_AccessKeyWatermark` / `Shell_AccessKeyWatermark` (RemEx-dk3p), each proven unreferenced by a whitespace-collapsed search across every `.cs` and `.axaml` — never by grepping the qualified `LocalizationService.Instance["Key"]` form, which line-wrapping defeats.
